pr_title: Fix Glances to use dedicated httpx client with longer timeout and surface API error messages
issue_title: Glances integration fails intermittently due to 5-second HTTP timeout
issue_body:
### The problem

The Glances integration uses `get_async_client` from `homeassistant.helpers.httpx_client` which appears to inherit a 5-second timeout. On systems where Glances takes longer than 5 seconds to return data (on complex or busy hosts), the fetch silently fails with an empty error message and the sensors go unavailable.

As shown in the debug logs below, successful fetches routinely take 3.8–4.9 seconds — leaving almost no margin before the timeout is hit. Any momentary slowness tips it over.

Ideally either the timeout could be higher or by expose this as a user-configurable option in the integration's config flow.

A secondary issue: when the timeout is hit, the error logged contains no message (`Error fetching glances - localhost data: `; note the empty string after the colon). The `GlancesApiConnectionError` message is only visible at DEBUG level. The error log would include the exception message to make this diagnosable without enabling debug logging.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.4.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Glances

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/glances/

pr_title: Fix derivative sensor staying unavailable after total_increasing reset
issue_title: Derivative Sensor is marked Unavailable after each midnight until a second sample is received that day
issue_body: ### The problem I realise there was MUCH discussion in the past about how to calculate and show 0 rate of change when Home Assistant only reports changes of data. I believe this is fixed for almost all cases. But in the case of a base cumulative sensor that briefly goes Unavailable when it resets to zero at midnight (such as the 7 sensors like `grid_exported_from_battery`, from the Teslemetry integration), there is a problem. Please look at the attached Excel. At midnight, the cumulative sensor shows Unavailable until 00:05, when a valid value is sent. For my example of misbehaviour for `grid_exported_from_battery`, the valid value is 0 as the battery won't export any kWh to the grid until 16:00 Unfortunately, **the Derivative sensor** based on this cumulative sensor **remains Unavailable all day until 16:05**, when a second valid value comes in. **I believe it should show 0 rate of change from 00:05 through 16:00** (rather than Unavailable): there is no updated value in HA, so it can be assumed that the cumulative value is still zero, so the rate of change should be zero. Looking later in the data, we see correct behaviour around 17:00 when the export ends abruptly. The derivative tails off across the 20-minute time window as you might expect. (In reality the power doesn't actually tail off, it stops suddenly, but I understand this representation). And we also see good behaviour after the brief Unavailable periods at 17:31 and 17:37: When the cumulative sensor goes Unavailable, the Derivative goes Unavailable as expected. When the cumulative sensor comes back, with the same value as before, the Derivative is correctly set to zero. This shows that the code doesn't need two valid values after **every** Unavailable period, **just the one at midnight** - so I think the issue may have something to do with the handling of the cumulative sensor's reset to zero being simultaneous with dealing with Unavailable. Unlike an Unavailable period during the day, the code has a previous valid value to fall back on. On the midnight reset, it may have discarded the pre-midnight value when it received the 00:05 zero. Happy to clarify anything if this is not clear. [Derivative Sensor problem.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28931090/Derivative.Sensor.problem.xlsx) ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2026.5.4 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? pr_title: Support Client ID Metadata Documents when verifying redirect_uri
issue_title: Auth advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported but never fetches the document — "Invalid redirect URI" for CIMD clients with cross-origin redirect_uri (Gemini Spark)
issue_body:
### The problem

The RFC 8414 metadata served at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` (added in #166220). Per the CIMD spec (draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document, adopted by MCP), a client that sees this flag presents a URL-shaped `client_id` and expects the authorization server to fetch that URL — a JSON document containing `redirect_uris` — to validate its redirect.

Home Assistant never fetches the document. `indieauth.verify_redirect_uri()` accepts a redirect_uri only if it is (a) same scheme+netloc as the `client_id`, (b) on the hardcoded companion-app allowlist, or (c) published as an HTML `<link rel="redirect_uri">` tag at the client_id URL (`fetch_redirect_uris()` runs an HTML parser only). A JSON CIMD document yields nothing, so any CIMD client whose redirect_uri is not same-origin with its client_id is rejected: login succeeds, then `login_flow.py` returns 403 "Invalid redirect URI" ([source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/auth/login_flow.py#L309-L312)).

Claude.ai and ChatGPT MCP connectors work only by coincidence — their client_id and redirect_uri are same-origin, so check (a) passes and the missing fetch never matters. Google Gemini Spark's "custom connected apps" (MCP) use `client_id = https://accountlinking.google.com/clientidmetadata/...` with a redirect_uri on a different Google host, which the CIMD spec permits — so every Gemini Spark → Home Assistant OAuth attempt fails after login with "Invalid redirect URI".

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expose an MCP server on a Home Assistant instance (e.g. via Nabu Casa).
2. In the Gemini web app, add it as a custom connected app for Gemini Spark.
3. Gemini Spark discovers HA's OAuth metadata, redirects to `/auth/authorize` with a CIMD client_id.
4. Log in → "Error: Invalid redirect URI".

Suggested fix: in `fetch_redirect_uris()`, when the client_id URL responds with `application/json`, parse it as a CIMD document and exact-match the request's redirect_uri against its `redirect_uris` array (keeping the existing HTML link-tag path for IndieAuth clients). Alternatively, stop advertising `client_id_metadata_document_supported` until it is implemented.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.7.2 (the code paths above are unchanged on `dev`)

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

None — CIMD fetching has never been implemented; the advertisement flag was added in #166220.

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Auth

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/auth/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Frontend shows "Error: Invalid redirect URI" after successful login.
Client ID observed in the authorize URL (reported downstream):
https://accountlinking.google.com/clientidmetadata/user_bound_provider/user_bound_custom-mcp-<id>-<instance>_ui_nabu_casa
```

### Additional information

Downstream report with full analysis: homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp#1787. The comment added in #166220 acknowledges the gap: "The metadata document is not actually fetched as IndieAuth doesn't require it." That was safe for same-origin clients (claude.ai, ChatGPT — see #153820), but Google Gemini Spark is the first major MCP client to rely on the advertised CIMD behavior with a cross-origin redirect_uri.

pr_title: Fix Growatt V1 total output power
issue_title: Growatt OpenAPI total output power becomes zero while plant power continues
issue_body:
### The problem

With Growatt API-token authentication, the plant-total output-power sensor can
become `0 W` while the plant is still producing and Growatt's own portal still
shows non-zero power.

On 2026-07-14 in Europe/Amsterdam, Home Assistant changed the total output
power from `1560 W` at `17:59:05` to `0 W` at `18:04:05`. At `18:56:31`, the
Growatt portal still showed `880.6 W`. The daily-energy value continued rising
from `19.0 kWh` after the power sensor became zero to `20.3 kWh`.

Direct OpenAPI requests with the same token and plant at approximately the
same time reproduced the disagreement. Relevant fields are shown below with
identifiers redacted:

```text
GET /v1/plant/data?plant_id=<redacted>
error_code: 0
current_power: 0
today_energy: 20.3
total_energy: 22401.1
last_update: 2026-07-14 19:10:16

GET /v1/plant/power?plant_id=<redacted>&date=2026-07-14
18:00  1495.4 W
18:30  1283.5 W
18:45  1045.5 W
18:55   880.6 W
19:00   780.0 W
19:10   415.7 W
```

The `880.6 W` entry exactly matches the Growatt portal. Recorder history from
2026-07-05 through 2026-07-14 shows the plant-total sensor dropping abruptly
to zero around 18:00-18:04 every day, followed by approximately 1.4-2.2 kWh of
additional daily generation.

This was not a rate-limit event: both OpenAPI calls succeeded and the energy
entities continued updating.

The current V1 total coordinator calls `plant_energy_overview()` and maps its
`current_power` field to `invTodayPpv`. The pinned `growattServer==2.1.0`
library also provides `plant_power_overview()`, which calls the documented
`/v1/plant/power` endpoint. Growatt documents that endpoint as returning the
daily power series in watts and limits it to one request every five minutes,
matching the coordinator interval.

The plant's connected inverter is returned as OpenAPI device type `1`, which
Home Assistant currently skips for a device coordinator. That leaves the
plant-total sensor as the only available production-power entity. However,
the endpoint disagreement is a plant-total issue and is independently
reproducible without adding type-1 device support.

Expected behavior: the plant-total output-power entity should use a recent
valid value from the plant power series when available, while retaining a safe
fallback if that endpoint is unavailable or stale.

Related reports:

- #120051 reports Growatt current power constantly zero while OpenAPI exposes
  production data; it was closed as stale.
- #173148 confirms that OpenAPI device types including type `1` are discovered
  but skipped.
- Historical community reports show the same aggregate-zero versus graph-data
  disagreement on other Growatt installations.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Growatt

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/growatt_server/

### Diagnostics information

Diagnostics contain installation identifiers and are not pasted publicly.
Relevant behavior and redacted endpoint results are included above. I can
provide additional redacted diagnostics if requested.

Not applicable; the integration is configured through a config entry using API
token authentication.

No Growatt exception or rate-limit message occurred during the reproduced
period.

### Additional information

The API token, plant ID, and device serial have been redacted. A fix with unit
tests is being prepared against the current `dev` branch.

pr_title: Use BaseException instead of bare except in rainforest_raven
issue_title: Bare except clause in rainforest_raven coordinator
issue_body:
### The problem

**The problem**

`_get_device` in the rainforest_raven coordinator uses a bare `except:`
around the device connect/sync sequence:

```python
try:
    async with asyncio.timeout(5):
        await device.open()
        await device.synchronize()
        self._device_info = await device.get_device_info()
except:
    await device.abort()
    raise
```

A bare `except:` also catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit`,
which isn't the intent here — the block just needs to abort the
device and re-raise whatever error actually occurred. This should be
`except BaseException:` (or restructured as a `finally` block) to
make the intent explicit and match the project's usual linting
standards.

lines 136-142.

pr_title: Tolerate unloading a never-loaded config entry in EntityComponent
issue_title: Silently failed forwarded platform setup wedges config entries into non-recoverable FAILED_UNLOAD on next unload
issue_body:
### The problem

When a forwarded platform's setup fails, the failure is silently discarded: `_async_forward_entry_setups_locked` gathers the per-platform setup tasks and ignores their results, and for forwarded domains `ConfigEntry.async_setup` explicitly does not store a failed result as state ("Only store setup result as state if it was not forwarded"). The owning config entry therefore ends up `LOADED` while one of its platforms was never registered in that domain's `EntityComponent` (`self._platforms`).

Everything appears to work — until the entry is next unloaded (user reload, reauth, options flow, or an integration-triggered reload). `EntityComponent.async_unload_entry` then raises `ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")` for the phantom platform, `config_entries` converts that into a failed unload, and the entry lands in **`FAILED_UNLOAD` — a non-recoverable state**. Every subsequent reload attempt raises `OperationNotAllowed`; the only way out is restarting Home Assistant.

The net effect: a transient, invisible platform setup failure (e.g. a flaky cloud API during one reload) converts a later, perfectly normal unload into a restart-only outage. There is nothing to unload for the phantom platform, so failing the whole unload — and wedging the entry — serves no purpose.

This is not integration-specific. Reports of the same chain across the years:

- tibber `notify`: #166228 (2026-03-27 comment has the full chain: API 504s → `Error unloading entry Tibber for notify` / `ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!` → `cannot be unloaded because it is in the non recoverable state ConfigEntryState.FAILED_UNLOAD`) — issue closed after an unrelated polling rework, wedge mechanism not addressed
- esphome `assist_satellite`: #159949 — reporter explicitly identified `helpers.entity_component.async_unload_entry` as not handling never-loaded entries; closed stale
- tibber `sensor`: #90180 (2023.3) — same `ValueError` on reload; closed stale

I hit it again this week on 2026.6.4 (tibber, `notify` platform), and the relevant code is unchanged on `dev`.

A fix PR follows shortly: make `EntityComponent.async_unload_entry` log a warning and return `True` when the entry was never registered, so the unload completes and the entry remains reloadable. (The deeper issue — forwarded setup failures being discarded without marking the entry — may deserve separate discussion, but the unload-side fix removes the restart-only failure mode.)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.6.4 (mechanism verified unchanged on current `dev`)

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Not a regression — the raise has been in `EntityComponent.async_unload_entry` for many years (reports go back to 2023.3, #90180).

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Not integration-specific — `homeassistant.helpers.entity_component` / config entry unload flow. Observed via `tibber` (notify platform); previously reported via `esphome` (assist_satellite) and `tibber` (sensor).

### Link to integration documentation on our website

n/a (core helpers)

### Diagnostics information

n/a — the failure is in core helpers; the traceback below identifies it precisely.

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
ERROR (MainThread) [custom_components.tibber] Error unloading entry Tibber for notify
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 1034, in async_unload
    result = await component.async_unload_entry(hass, self)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/notify/__init__.py", line 125, in async_unload_entry
    return await hass.data[DATA_COMPONENT].async_unload_entry(entry)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_component.py", line 201, in async_unload_entry
    raise ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")
ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!

-- and on any subsequent reload attempt: --

homeassistant.config_entries.OperationNotAllowed: The config entry 'Tibber' (tibber) with entry_id '<redacted>' cannot be unloaded because it is in the non recoverable state ConfigEntryState.FAILED_UNLOAD
```

### Additional information

Note on the traceback above: the `custom_components.tibber` logger name is an artefact of reproducing with a copy of the core integration; the identical chain occurs with the built-in integration — see the March traceback in #166228.

Reproduction sketch (any integration with forwarded platforms):

1. Make one forwarded platform's `async_setup_entry` raise once during entry setup (e.g. patch the notify platform to raise) — the entry still reaches `LOADED`; only an "Error setting up entry X for <platform>" line is logged and nothing marks the entry.
2. Reload the entry → `ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!` from `EntityComponent.async_unload_entry` → entry state `FAILED_UNLOAD`.
3. Reload again → `OperationNotAllowed`; only a core restart recovers.

Related open feature request acknowledging there is no runtime escape from `FAILED_UNLOAD`: #151771.

pr_title: Fix SMTP attaching valid images as files when content sniffing fails
issue_title: SMTP does not recognise image attachments generated with action: camera.snapshot
issue_body:
### The problem

Images generated by action: camera.snapshot are not recognised as images when attached to email notifications. as a result they are attached as application/octet-stream instead of image/jpeg.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

SMTP

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/smtp/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
action: notify.mail_sender
data:
  message: Doorphone Motion Detected
  data:
    images:
      - /config/www/snapshots/doorphone.jpg
```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
WARNING [homeassistant.components.smtp.helpers]
Attachment /config/www/snapshots/doorphone.jpg has an unknown MIME type. Falling back to file
```

### Additional information

Root cause
homeassistant.components.smtp.helpers.py _attach_file() does:

  attachment = MIMEImage(file_bytes)

which raises:

   TypeError: Could not guess image MIME subtype

for valid JPEGs.

The JPEG starts:

ffd8fffe00104c61766336322e32382e31303200...

i.e. JPEG SOI followed by a COM marker containing:

Lavc62.28.102

The file is valid and opens correctly with other applications.

Workaround
Fallback using mimetypes:

try:
    attachment = MIMEImage(file_bytes)
except TypeError:
    ctype, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(atch_name)
    if ctype and ctype.startswith("image/"):
        attachment = MIMEImage(
            file_bytes,
            _subtype=ctype.split("/", 1)[1],
        )
    else:
        attachment = MIMEApplication(
            file_bytes,
            Name=os.path.basename(atch_name),
        )

In addition, the warning text is slightly misleading. The MIME type is known (image/jpeg from the filename); the problem is that MIMEImage cannot infer the subtype from the binary data. That distinction will probably help avoid people chasing the wrong cause.

pr_title: Fix swallowed exceptions in action handlers for Pushover
issue_title: Fix swallowed exceptions in pushover action handlers
issue_body:
The `pushover` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `notify.py`:**
- `(see source)` (notify.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

pr_title: idrive_e2: warmup loader caches to remove blocking listdir calls
issue_title: IDrive e2 blocks event loop with synchronous listdir/open calls during setup
issue_body:
### The problem

The IDrive e2 integration performs multiple synchronous blocking calls (`os.listdir`, `open`, `load_verify_locations`) inside the async event loop during `async_setup_entry`. These calls originate from `botocore`'s loader when `aiobotocore` creates the S3 client at `idrive_e2/__init__.py`, line 50.

This was previously visible in the logs attached to #165157, but that issue was about iDrive-side upload speed throttling and was closed without addressing the blocking calls.

The blocking calls occur on every startup/reload and produce multiple warnings:

- `listdir` on `/usr/local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/botocore/data` (loader scanning service directories)
- `listdir` on individual service subdirectories (e.g., `botocore/data/s3`)
- `open` on gzipped service definition files (e.g., `service-2.json.gz`)
- `load_verify_locations` loading SSL certificates

The root cause is in `aiobotocore`/`botocore` — the async `session.create_client()` internally calls botocore's loader which performs synchronous filesystem I/O without running it in an executor. Since `create_client` returns an async context manager, wrapping it with `async_add_executor_job` is not straightforward. This likely needs to be fixed upstream in aiobotocore, or worked around by pre-warming botocore's service model cache in an executor before client creation.

The Cloudflare R2 integration has the same code pattern and would have the same issue.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.4.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

IDrive e2

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/idrive_e2/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

For developers, please see https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/asyncio_blocking_operations/#listdir

2026-04-02 13:37:04.332 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.util.loop] Detected blocking call to listdir with args ('/usr/local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/botocore/data/meteringmarketplace',) inside the event loop by integration 'idrive_e2' at homeassistant/components/idrive_e2/__init__.py, line 50: client = await session.create_client( (offender: /usr/local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/botocore/loaders.py, line 312: api_versions = os.listdir(full_dirname))

2026-04-02 13:37:06.777 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.util.loop] Detected blocking call to open with args ('/usr/local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/botocore/data/s3/2006-03-01/service-2.json.gz', 'rb') inside the event loop by integration 'idrive_e2' at homeassistant/components/idrive_e2/__init__.py, line 50: client = await session.create_client( (offender: /usr/local/lib/python3.14/gzip.py, line 208: fileobj = self.myfileobj = builtins.open(filename, mode or 'rb'))
```

pr_title: Show artwork and a play button when opening a Sonos music library album
issue_title: Sonos: opening a music library album in the media browser shows no artwork or play button
issue_body: ### The problem In the Sonos media browser, the Albums list shows each album with its cover art and a play button. Opening one of those albums shows only a bare track list: no cover art and no play button for the album itself. Steps to reproduce: 1. Set up a music library on the Sonos system, if you do not already have one (Sonos app, Settings, System, Music Library, then add a folder of music). This affects the music library, not favorites or streaming services. 2. Go to Settings, Devices and services, Entities, and click one of your Sonos media players to open its dialog. 3. Click the folder icon in the player controls to browse media. 4. Open Music Library, then Albums. Each album shows its cover and a play button, and the play button works. 5. Click one of the albums to open it. The album view has only the list of tracks. There is no cover art for the album and no play button for it. Expected: opening an album shows the album's cover art and a play button, matching how the album appears in the Albums list. This is the same view with a local patch applied: Reproduced on core-2026.5.1 and on current `dev`. ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2026.5.1 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant Container ### Integration causing the issue Sonos ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? ```txt Nothing is logged. ``` ### Additional information **Cause** `build_item_response` fills in the album container's own fields, and the values it passes do not match what the helpers expect: | Call | Passes | Expects | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `can_play(payload["search_type"])` | `MediaType.ALBUM`, `"album"` | a key of `SONOS_TO_MEDIA_TYPES`, such as a DIDL class | `False` | | `get_thumbnail_url(search_type, ...)` | `SONOS_ALBUM`, `"albums"` | a `MediaType` | image request returns 500 | | `can_expand(payload["search_type"])` | `MediaType.ALBUM`, `"album"` | an `"A:ALBUM"` style key | `False` | `can_play` returning `False` is what removes the header from the album view, and the header is what carries both the cover art and the play button. The child items in the same response are unaffected, because `item_payload` passes the DIDL class (`can_play(item.item_class, item_id=content_id)`), which maps correctly. That is why an album is playable from the Albums list but not from inside the album. `MediaType.ALBUM` is listed in `PLAYABLE_MEDIA_TYPES`, so albums are clearly intended to be playable here. **Second defect behind the same symptom** Even with `can_play` corrected, the cover would still fail to load when Home Assistant is reached by a URL that is not internal, because the image request carries the Sonos search type: ``` container thumbnail: /api/media_player_proxy/media_player.main/browse_media/albums/A:ALBUM/Up/Peter%2520Gabriel GET -> 500 same album's tile in the Albums list: .../browse_media/album/A:ALBUM/Up/Peter%2520Gabriel GET -> 200, image/jpg ``` `async_get_browse_image` matches on `MediaType.ALBUM` and `MediaType.ARTIST`, so `"albums"` matches nothing, it returns `(None, None)`, and the proxy view turns that into a 500. This part only shows up when `is_internal_request(hass)` is False, since internal requests return the speaker's direct art URL and never use the proxy. **Possible fix** Pass each helper the vocabulary it expects: a `MediaType` to `get_thumbnail_url`, and a Sonos search type to `can_play`. `get_media` already normalises either vocabulary, so the lookup itself is unaffected. One caveat found while trying this: because the same `can_play` call covers every container, correcting it in place also marks the library listings themselves (Albums, Artists, Genres and so on) as playable, which puts a play button on each of those listings. Only a single resolved album should become playable, so the correction needs to be scoped to that case rather than applied to every container. **Relationship to #173330** Separate from #173330, which fixes browse images for tracks and does not touch these lines.

pr_title: Derive the WiiM UPnP event callback host from the device route instead of the Home Assistant URL
issue_title: WiiM advertises an unreachable UPnP event callback host on multi-homed hosts, silently disabling eventing
issue_body:
### The problem

On a multi-homed host, the WiiM integration can advertise a UPnP event callback address the device cannot route to. The GENA subscription succeeds, so nothing errors and nothing is logged, but no NOTIFY is ever delivered: the media player entity shows no `media_title` / `media_artist` / `entity_picture` and its transport state never updates. It looks like a metadata bug, but no event arrives at all.

The callback host comes from the Home Assistant URL:

```python
# homeassistant/components/wiim/util.py
def get_homeassistant_local_host(hass: HomeAssistant) -> str:
    base_url = get_url(hass, prefer_external=False)
```

With no internal URL configured, `get_url` falls back to `hass.config.api.local_ip`, which comes from `network.async_get_source_ip`:

```python
# homeassistant/components/network/__init__.py
return source_ip if source_ip in all_ipv4s else all_ipv4s[0]
```

If the routed source address is not itself an enabled adapter, the routed answer is discarded and the **first enabled adapter** is returned. That address has no relationship to the route to the device. In my case it was a Docker network declared `internal: true`, which no LAN device can reach, and the SDK used it verbatim as the notify server source.

My environment (addresses sanitized, topology preserved):

```
internal_url = None
configured_adapters = ["eth1", "eth2"]

default via 192.168.20.1 dev eth0   src 192.168.20.5   (NOT an enabled adapter)
192.168.30.0/24      dev eth1       src 192.168.30.5   (device lives here)
172.30.33.0/24       dev eth2       src 172.30.33.5    (docker bridge, internal: true)
```

Routed source `192.168.20.5` is not in `all_ipv4s`, so `all_ipv4s[0]` wins and `172.30.33.5` is advertised to the device at `192.168.30.99`.

Suggested fix: resolve the callback host per device from the route to that device, which `dlna_dmr` already does with the same `async_upnp_client` dependency:

```python
# homeassistant/components/dlna_dmr/media_player.py
_, event_ip = await async_get_local_ip(location, self.hass.loop)
```

`async_setup_entry` already builds the device's `upnp_location`, so it is a drop-in there.

Workaround for anyone hitting this: deselect the unreachable adapter under Settings > System > Network so it cannot be chosen as `all_ipv4s[0]`, and/or set an explicit internal URL on an interface the devices can reach.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.7.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

WiiM

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/wiim/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
INFO [wiim.sdk] Device WiiM Pro: AiohttpNotifyServer for UPnP events started at: http://172.30.33.5:50099/notify
INFO [wiim.sdk] Device WiiM Pro: Subscribed to available UPnP service events.
```

Over a full session with the device actively playing (debug logging enabled):

- `AVTransportURIMetaData` / `CurrentTrackMetaData` occurrences in the log: 0
- `Skipping polling due to recent UPnP event`: 0 (no event was ever received)
- `AVTransport.GetInfoEx` polls returning full metadata incl. `<upnp:albumArtURI>`: present throughout

### Additional information

The device itself is fine: `getMetaInfo` over its HTTP API and `GetPositionInfo` over UPnP both return complete metadata on demand, and eventing works once the callback host is an address the device can route to (verified with the workaround above).

pr_title: Use dt_util system_timezone in remote_calendar diagnostics
issue_title: Avoid a naive `datetime.now()` in remote_calendar
issue_body:
The `remote_calendar` integration calls a naive `datetime.now()` (no time zone) directly, suppressing `home-assistant-enforce-naive-now`.

**Violations:**
- [`homeassistant/components/remote_calendar/diagnostics.py:22`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/165419f227d39b6a8b8ffd4b4ec7a68be400aecb/homeassistant/components/remote_calendar/diagnostics.py#L22)

pr_title: Fix loading IP bans without banned_at
issue_title: Missing banned_at in ip_bans.yaml prevents HTTP server from starting
issue_body:
### The problem

Home Assistant Core 2026.8.0 fails to start its HTTP server when `ip_bans.yaml` contains a valid IP address whose entry is empty or lacks the required `banned_at` field.

This leaves Core partially running, but makes the local frontend, Supervisor HTTP socket and Remote UI unavailable.

This appears to be the still-unhandled variant of #166979. It is also related to #157180 and PR #157232, but that fix only catches `ValueError` for malformed IP addresses.

## Reproduction

Add the following to `/config/ip_bans.yaml`:

```yaml
45.91.64.6:
```

Restart Home Assistant Core.

The subsequent Supervisor HTTP socket setup also fails because the aiohttp runner was not initialized:

```text
RuntimeError: Call runner.setup() before making a site
```
## Expected behavior

Malformed or incomplete entries in `ip_bans.yaml` should be logged and skipped. They should never prevent the entire HTTP server from starting.

Validation should cover at least:

* a non-mapping or empty entry;
* a missing `banned_at` field;
* an invalid `banned_at` value;
* an invalid IP address.

## Actual behavior

The uncaught `KeyError` aborts HTTP server startup and makes all web-based recovery paths unavailable.

## Recovery

Renaming or deleting `ip_bans.yaml` from the host shell and restarting Core restores access.

pr_title: Avoid a naive datetime.now() in broadlink
issue_title: Avoid a naive `datetime.now()` in broadlink
issue_body:
The `broadlink` integration calls a naive `datetime.now()` (no time zone) directly, suppressing `home-assistant-enforce-naive-now`.

**Violations:**
- [`homeassistant/components/broadlink/heartbeat.py:34`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/165419f227d39b6a8b8ffd4b4ec7a68be400aecb/homeassistant/components/broadlink/heartbeat.py#L34)

**How to fix:**

Before replacing the call, check whether a naive datetime is actually needed:

1. **Relative time** (measuring a duration or time until an event): a datetime is not needed. Use `time.time()` (a float), e.g. `event_time - time.time()` instead of `event_time - datetime.now().timestamp()`. This is the most common case.
2. **A timezone-aware datetime is appropriate**: use `dt_util.now()` (local) or `dt_util.utcnow()` (UTC), importing `from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util`.
3. **A naive local datetime is genuinely required** (e.g. a 3rd-party library expects one): only then replace with `dt_util.naive_now()` and remove the `# pylint: disable=home-assistant-enforce-naive-now` suppression.

See the `homeassistant.util.dt.naive_now` docstring for details.

Part of home-assistant/epics#117

pr_title: Fix Statistics helper crash with sampling_size of 0
issue_title: Statistics helper: `Sampling size: 0` crashes setup and leaves an undeletable broken helper
issue_body:
### The problem

The Statistics helper's **Sampling size** field accepts `0` (the selector is `min=0`), but `0` crashes the sensor and produces a helper that:

- shows a red error with **no entity ID**,
- has an **empty preview** in the options dialog,
- and **cannot be deleted from the UI** (the Helpers row menu only shows Settings / Assign category — no Delete), because the entity never registers.

Setting Sampling size to any non-zero value works fine and un-breaks it, but there is no indication that `0` is invalid — the field happily accepts it and silently produces a wedged helper.

To reproduce:

1. Settings -> Devices & Services -> Helpers -> Create Helper -> **Statistics**.
2. Pick any numeric source, characteristic **Max value**, **Sampling size = 0**, Max age = 1:00:00.
3. The preview is empty; after saving, the helper shows a red error, no entity ID, and cannot be deleted from the UI.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Statistics

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/statistics

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# The helper is created through the UI; these are the resulting config entry
# options that trigger the problem.
entity_id: sensor.any_numeric_source
state_characteristic: value_max
sampling_size: 0
max_age:
  hours: 1
  minutes: 0
  seconds: 0
keep_last_sample: false
precision: 2
```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Setup:

ERROR [homeassistant.components.sensor] Error while setting up statistics platform for sensor: an integer is required
  File ".../statistics/sensor.py", line 689, in __init__
    self.states: deque[float | bool] = deque(maxlen=samples_max_buffer_size)
TypeError: an integer is required

Options preview:

  File ".../statistics/sensor.py", line 1084, in _update_extra_state_attributes
    len(self.states) / self._samples_max_buffer_size, 2
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

### Additional information

**Root cause**

The config-flow field is a `NumberSelector(min=0, ...)`, which returns a **float**. In `async_setup_entry` (`components/statistics/sensor.py`):

```python
sampling_size = entry.options.get(CONF_SAMPLES_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE)   # e.g. 0.0 (float)
if sampling_size:          # 0.0 is falsy -> the int() coercion below is skipped
    sampling_size = int(sampling_size)
...
samples_max_buffer_size=sampling_size,   # stays 0.0
```

- Non-zero values are truthy -> `int()`-coerced -> `deque(maxlen=100)` works, which is why normal helpers are fine.
- `0.0` is falsy -> coercion skipped -> `deque(maxlen=0.0)` in `__init__` raises `TypeError: an integer is required` -> setup fails -> no entity -> not deletable.
- The options preview does coerce to int, then hits `len(self.states) / self._samples_max_buffer_size` = `... / 0` -> `ZeroDivisionError`.

**Suggested fix**

Any of, ideally the first plus one of the others:

- `NumberSelector(min=1, ...)` so the UI cannot accept `0`.
- `if sampling_size is not None:` instead of `if sampling_size:` so `0.0` still coerces to `int`.
- Guard the percentage line (`if self._samples_max_buffer_size:`) — it currently only checks `is not None`, not `0`.

pr_title: Fix ESPHome climate target temperature handling in auto mode
issue_title: ESPHome: temperature attribute is null for single-setpoint climate entities in auto mode
issue_body:
### The problem

For an ESPHome climate entity with no two-point target temperature support, the temperature attribute is null whenever hvac_mode is auto, even though the entity advertises ClimateEntityFeature.TARGET_TEMPERATURE. climate.set_temperature still works in auto and the device applies it — only the read-back is broken, which makes the temperature dial read-only in the UI.

Cause, in homeassistant/components/esphome/climate.py:
```py
def target_temperature(self) -> float | None:
    if (
        not self._feature_flags & (REQUIRES_TWO_POINT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE | SUPPORTS_TWO_POINT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE)
        and self.hvac_mode != HVACMode.AUTO   # <-- excludes AUTO here
    ):
        return self._state.target_temperature
    if self.hvac_mode == HVACMode.HEAT:
        return self._state.target_temperature_low
    if self.hvac_mode == HVACMode.COOL:
        return self._state.target_temperature_high
    return None   # single-setpoint device in AUTO falls through to here
```
A device with neither two-point flag has no target_temperature_low/high, so it should never fall through to None. This was introduced in [#151897](https://github.com/eigger/esphome_samsung_hvac_bus/issues/151897), which handled ESPHome's thermostat component (where AUTO means heat/cool changeover and needs a low/high pair) but didn't account for real A/C devices where AUTO means "unit picks the mode" with a single setpoint.

Regressed between 2025.9.0 (works) and 2025.10.0 (broken).

Suggested fix — drop the AUTO exclusion, since it's unreachable correctly for single-setpoint devices:
```py
-        if (
-            not self._feature_flags & (REQUIRES_TWO_POINT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE | SUPPORTS_TWO_POINT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE)
-            and self.hvac_mode != HVACMode.AUTO
-        ):
+        if not self._feature_flags & (REQUIRES_TWO_POINT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE | SUPPORTS_TWO_POINT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE):
             return self._state.target_temperature
```
Example state while in auto:
```
temperature: null   # expected 24.0
supported_features: 441   # TARGET_TEMPERATURE set, TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE not set
```

core-2026.8.1

Home Assistant OS

pr_title: `errors` could be `None` in Shelly Wall Display status
issue_title: Shelly: one "errors": null aborts the entire sensor platform
issue_body:
### The problem

**Title:** Shelly: entire sensor platform fails to set up when a component reports `"errors": null`

### The problem

`sensor.py` treats the RPC component field `errors` as always iterable:

```python
# homeassistant/components/shelly/sensor.py:1236
DRIVER_MISSING_ERROR in status[key].get("errors", [])
```

`dict.get(key, default)` only returns the default when the key is **absent**. A Shelly device is free to send the key present with an explicit `null`, in which case `.get("errors", [])` returns `None` and the membership test raises `TypeError`.

Because this runs inside `removal_condition` during `async_setup_rpc_attribute_entities`, the exception propagates out of `async_setup_entry` and **the entire sensor platform for that config entry is aborted** — not just the offending entity. Every other platform on the same device (switch, light, media_player, binary_sensor, update) sets up normally, so the device looks online and healthy while all of its sensors sit at `unavailable` indefinitely.

The condition was introduced in #170900 (merged 2026-05-23), which added the temperature/humidity `removal_condition` lambdas.

### Reproduction

My Shelly Wall Display intermittently emits `"errors": null` on `temperature:0` and `humidity:0`. Straight from the device's own `Shelly.GetStatus`:

```json
{
  "temperature:0": { "id": 0, "tC": 27.6, "tF": 82, "errors": null },
  "humidity:0":    { "id": 0, "rh": 34.5,            "errors": null }
}
```

Whenever a platform setup lands while the payload is in that state, the crash is 100% reproducible: it fired on a Home Assistant restart and again on a `homeassistant.reload_config_entry` for the same entry. Rebooting the device removed the `errors` key entirely, after which a reload restored all four sensors. No firmware change was involved at any point.

Note the device had been up 29.9 hours with the null present while the sensors worked fine — `removal_condition` is only evaluated at setup, so the field's state matters solely at the moment a setup runs. That is why this presents as random and why it surfaces on restarts.

This is **not** firmware-specific. I originally believed device firmware 2.7.4 fixed it (2.7.3 appeared to emit the null and 2.7.4 not to), but the null reappeared on 2.7.4, which is the latest available (`Shelly.CheckForUpdate` returns `{}`).

### Suggested fix

```python
DRIVER_MISSING_ERROR in (status[key].get("errors") or [])
```

A device sending `"errors": null` is well-formed; Home Assistant should not lose a whole platform over it. It may be worth auditing other `.get(..., [])` / `.get(..., {})` calls on RPC payload fields in this integration for the same present-but-null assumption.

pr_title: Add support for inverted output in Shelly climate entity
issue_title: Shelly Wall Display X1i reports reversed `hvac_action` when thermostat output is inverted
issue_body:
### The problem

## The problem

I am using a Shelly Wall Display X1i as a heating thermostat with its internal relay configured with inverted output logic.

The physical heating system requires the following logic:

* Heating demand → relay output OFF
* No heating demand → relay output ON

The Shelly thermostat itself operates correctly with this configuration.

However, the Home Assistant Shelly integration reports the `hvac_action` backwards.

Example:

Home Assistant climate entity:

```text
entity_id: climate.olohuone_shellywalldisplay_olohuone
state: heat

current_temperature: 25.4
temperature: 20.5
current_humidity: 46
hvac_action: heating
```

At this moment the room temperature is 25.4 °C and the target is 20.5 °C, so there is clearly no heating demand. The physical relay is ON, which with the configured inverted output means heating is disabled.

The Shelly RPC status at the same moment is:

```json
"thermostat:0": {
  "id": 0,
  "enable": true,
  "target_C": 20.5,
  "target_F": 69,
  "current_C": 25.4,
  "current_F": 78,
  "output": true,
  "errors": [],
  "schedules": {
    "enable": false
  }
}
```

Home Assistant nevertheless reports:

```text
hvac_action: heating
```

The expected value in this situation is:

```text
hvac_action: idle
```

When heating demand is created by raising the target temperature above the current temperature, the Shelly output changes according to the inverted relay configuration, but Home Assistant reports the opposite HVAC action.

## Expected behavior

Home Assistant should report the logical thermostat action rather than assuming that:

```text
output == true → heating
output == false → idle
```

When the Shelly thermostat output is configured as inverted, `hvac_action` should take this inversion into account.

The Shelly device itself controls the heating correctly. Only the Home Assistant `hvac_action` representation appears to be reversed.

## Possible cause

The current Shelly `RpcClimate.hvac_action` implementation in:

```text
homeassistant/components/shelly/climate.py
```

appears to determine the HVAC action directly from the thermostat `output` value:

```python
if not self.status["output"]:
    return HVACAction.IDLE

return (
    HVACAction.COOLING
    if self._thermostat_type == "cooling"
    else HVACAction.HEATING
)
```

This appears not to account for a Shelly thermostat configured with inverted output.

## Device

Shelly Wall Display X1i

Thermostat uses the Wall Display internal relay as actuator.

Output inversion is enabled because the connected heating actuator requires power to disable heating and no power to enable heating.

## Home Assistant installation

Home Assistant OS

## Integration causing the issue

Shelly

## Home Assistant Core version

2026.8.1

## Shelly firmware version

2.7.4

## Additional information

The climate entity otherwise works correctly:

* current temperature is correct
* target temperature is correct
* humidity is correct
* 0.5 °C target temperature step is correct
* changing the target temperature from Home Assistant correctly updates the Shelly thermostat

Only the reported `hvac_action` appears to be inverted.

### Description

With Supervisor using the Unix socket to communicate with Core, we don't use a in-band authentication anymore. This makes the refresh token actually a liability: If someone gets hold of it, they get full admin access through the regular http port.

So far the TCP/IP communication was still preferred. Only with https://github.com/home-assistant/supervisor/pull/6815 Unix socket communication will become the default for Core 2026.5.1 and newer.

Let's remove the refresh token and don't hand it to the Supervisor anymore.

issue_title: Split user flow init and data submission in geonetnz_quakes config flow tests
issue_body:
The `geonetnz_quakes` integration's config flow tests start the user step with `data` already prefilled. In real life a user cannot start a flow with data prefilled, so tests should split initiating the flow (`async_init`) from submitting the data (`async_configure`).

**Violations:**
- [`tests/components/geonetnz_quakes/test_config_flow.py:28`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/components/geonetnz_quakes/test_config_flow.py#L28)
- [`tests/components/geonetnz_quakes/test_config_flow.py:96`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/components/geonetnz_quakes/test_config_flow.py#L96)

**How to fix:**

For each flagged `async_init` call, remove the `data=` argument (and the `# pylint: disable=home-assistant-tests-user-flow-no-data` suppression), assert the flow shows the user form (`FlowResultType.FORM`), then submit the input through a follow-up `hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(result["flow_id"], user_input=...)` call. This mirrors what a real user does: open the flow, then fill in the form.

pr_title: Avoid a naive datetime.now() in twitter
issue_title: Avoid a naive `datetime.now()` in twitter
issue_body:
The `twitter` integration calls a naive `datetime.now()` (no time zone) directly, suppressing `home-assistant-enforce-naive-now`.

**Violations:**
- [`homeassistant/components/twitter/notify.py:236`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/165419f227d39b6a8b8ffd4b4ec7a68be400aecb/homeassistant/components/twitter/notify.py#L236)

**How to fix:**

Before replacing the call, check whether a naive datetime is actually needed:

1. **Relative time** (measuring a duration or time until an event): a datetime is not needed. Use `time.time()` (a float), e.g. `event_time - time.time()` instead of `event_time - datetime.now().timestamp()`. This is the most common case.
2. **A timezone-aware datetime is appropriate**: use `dt_util.now()` (local) or `dt_util.utcnow()` (UTC), importing `from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util`.
3. **A naive local datetime is genuinely required** (e.g. a 3rd-party library expects one): only then replace with `dt_util.naive_now()` and remove the `# pylint: disable=home-assistant-enforce-naive-now` suppression.

See the `homeassistant.util.dt.naive_now` docstring for details.

pr_title: Fix inconsistent OpenGarage toggle behavior
issue_title: Cover toggle OpenGarage cover toggle fails
issue_body:
### The problem

Calling `cover.toggle` on my OpenGarage entity frequently results in a silent failure. The garage door does not respond to the toggle and there are no associated error logs. Running `cover.close` works just fine, and HA always has the correct state of the garage door (open or closed), so it's not confused about the door state.

This seems to be somewhat time dependent: if I haven't used HA to open the garage in a while, `cover.toggle` is likely to fail. But once it starts working, it works consistently for some period of time (hours) before it starts to fail again.

I've looked through the implementations of [cover](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/cover) and [opengarage](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/opengarage), and there's one thing I find suspicious. The cover toggle code was https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/59233 to only [toggle closed if the last toggle direction was open](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e19c6ac0118f81a2b2b5a8e9ab6f741c48c064ee/homeassistant/components/cover/__init__.py#L442).

This matches my experience of having much more trouble toggling closed than toggling open (I can't recall if toggling open is a problem). But I can't deterministically trigger the bug based on this logic, i.e., by toggling the cover closed, then manually opening outside of HA, then trying to toggle closed again. I don't understand how integrations store state such as `self._cover_is_last_toggle_direction_open` over time, possibly there's some time-based aspect to how this is updated.

pr_title: Split WebDAV config flow test submissions
issue_title: Split user flow init and data submission in webdav config flow tests
issue_body:
The `webdav` integration's config flow tests start the user step with `data` already prefilled. In real life a user cannot start a flow with data prefilled, so tests should split initiating the flow (`async_init`) from submitting the data (`async_configure`).

**Violations:**
- [`tests/components/webdav/test_config_flow.py:59`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/components/webdav/test_config_flow.py#L59)
- [`tests/components/webdav/test_config_flow.py:106`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/components/webdav/test_config_flow.py#L106)
- [`tests/components/webdav/test_config_flow.py:144`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/tests/components/webdav/test_config_flow.py#L144)

**How to fix:**

For each flagged `async_init` call, remove the `data=` argument (and the `# pylint: disable=home-assistant-tests-user-flow-no-data` suppression), assert the flow shows the user form (`FlowResultType.FORM`), then submit the input through a follow-up `hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(result["flow_id"], user_input=...)` call. This mirrors what a real user does: open the flow, then fill in the form.

When I use cursor to call the MCP service, it is normal and the request parameters are as follows:


```
2025-05-24 00:23:37.455 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.mcp_server.server] Tool call: HassClimateSetTemperature({'area': 'bedroom', 'temperature': 25})

```

pr_title: Abode: report change setting failures
issue_title: Fix swallowed exceptions in abode action handlers
issue_body:
The `abode` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `services.py`:**
- `_change_setting` (services.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

pr_title: Fix recorder.purge_entities dropping group entities from the purge set
issue_title: Recorder purge_entities does not purge history for group.* entity_id (group states remain untouched)
issue_body:
### The problem

When calling `recorder.purge_entities` with `entity_id` containing a `group.*` entity, Home Assistant does not delete any rows for that group entity from the `states` table. The group entity has its own entry in `states_meta` and a very large number of `states` rows, including rows older than the requested retention period. The purge task runs and deletes rows for other entities, but never targets the group’s `metadata_id`, so the group’s history remains unchanged.

This appears to be caused by group expansion during entity_id processing, where the group entity_id is expanded to its members and the group entity_id itself is not included in the purge target set.

`components / recorder / services.py / _async_handle_purge_entities_service(...)` generates the list of entities by calling `homeassistant.helpers.service.async_extract_entity_ids(service)` and leaves `expand_group` parameter to the default value, which is `True`:
`async def async_extract_entity_ids(service_call: ServiceCall, expand_group: bool = True) -> set[str]:...`

pr_title: Add additional sun triggers and conditions
issue_title: Add additional sun-based triggers and conditions
issue_body:
In 2026.7 we added the sun triggers and conditions we deemed higher priority. Through this task, we'll add the remaining lower priority ones.

In addition to the specified options, the triggers should also receive the ability to set a time-based offset (see #175828).

##### Triggers
 
| Key | Title | Description | Spec | Options |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sun.golden_hour_started` | Golden hour started | Triggers when golden hour starts, in the morning, the evening, or either. | Morning: elevation reaches -4° while rising. Evening: elevation reaches 6° while descending. With `any`, fires at both crossings. | `period`: `any` (default), `morning`, `evening` |
| `sun.golden_hour_ended` | Golden hour ended | Triggers when golden hour ends, in the morning, the evening, or either. | Morning: elevation reaches 6° while rising. Evening: elevation reaches -4° while descending. With `any`, fires at both crossings. | `period`: `any` (default), `morning`, `evening` |
| `sun.blue_hour_started` | Blue hour started | Triggers when blue hour starts, in the morning, the evening, or either. | Morning: elevation reaches -6° while rising. Evening: elevation reaches -4° while descending. With `any`, fires at both crossings. | `period`: `any` (default), `morning`, `evening` |
| `sun.blue_hour_ended` | Blue hour ended | Triggers when blue hour ends, in the morning, the evening, or either. | Morning: elevation reaches -4° while rising. Evening: elevation reaches -6° while descending. With `any`, fires at both crossings. | `period`: `any` (default), `morning`, `evening` |
| `sun.midnight_sun_started` | Midnight sun started | Triggers when the midnight sun period starts and the sun stops setting. | Sun stops setting; stays above the horizon for 24h. | — |
| `sun.midnight_sun_ended` | Midnight sun ended | Triggers when the midnight sun period ends and the sun sets again. | Sun sets again after a midnight sun period. | — |
| `sun.polar_night_started` | Polar night started | Triggers when the polar night period starts and the sun stops rising. | Sun stops rising; stays below the horizon for 24h. | — |
| `sun.polar_night_ended` | Polar night ended | Triggers when the polar night period ends and the sun rises again. | Sun rises again after a polar night period. | — |
 
##### Conditions
 
| Key | Title | Description | Spec | Options |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sun.is_golden_hour` | It is golden hour | Tests if it is golden hour, optionally for a specific period. | Elevation between -4° and 6°. | `period`: `any` (default), `morning`, `evening` |
| `sun.is_blue_hour` | It is blue hour | Tests if it is blue hour, optionally for a specific period. | Elevation between -6° and -4°. | `period`: `any` (default), `morning`, `evening` |
| `sun.is_midnight_sun` | It is midnight sun | Tests if it is midnight sun. | Sun stays above the horizon for 24h. | — |
| `sun.is_polar_night` | It is polar night | Tests if it is polar night. | Sun stays below the horizon for 24h. | — |

pr_title: Fix TemperatureOffset native min/max unit conversion for Matter thermostats
issue_title: Issues with Matter LocalTemperatureCalibration attribute
issue_body:
### The problem

Prior to cluster revision 7 of this Themostat cluster specification the value of this `LocalTemperatureCalibration` attribute was constrained to a range of -2.5°C to 2.5°C. 

- In revisions ≤ 6, the attribute could only contain calibration offsets between -2.5°C and +2.5°C.
- Starting with revision 7, this restriction was removed

| Matter Version | Max Thermostat Cluster Revision | Main Changes |
|----------------|----------------------------------|--------------|
| 1.3            | 6                                | Minor improvements and groundwork for HVAC extensions |
| 1.4            | 7                                | Added **Presets**, **MatterScheduleConfiguration**, events, and thermostat suggestions |


The code here is incorrect because the limits range from -2.5 to 2.5 degrees for revisions < 7 (Matter 1.3).
This leads to error messages and tickets being created incorrectly by users.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f2d43193669db8501c4a53f2f1d635cfcf9d636b/homeassistant/components/matter/number.py#L287-L307

issue_title: Avoid a naive `datetime.now()` in image
issue_body:
The `image` integration calls a naive `datetime.now()` (no time zone) directly, suppressing `home-assistant-enforce-naive-now`.

**Violations:**

Before replacing the call, check whether a naive datetime is actually needed:

1. **Relative time** (measuring a duration or time until an event): a datetime is not needed. Use `time.time()` (a float), e.g. `event_time - time.time()` instead of `event_time - datetime.now().timestamp()`. This is the most common case.
2. **A timezone-aware datetime is appropriate**: use `dt_util.now()` (local) or `dt_util.utcnow()` (UTC), importing `from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util`.
3. **A naive local datetime is genuinely required** (e.g. a 3rd-party library expects one): only then replace with `dt_util.naive_now()` and remove the `# pylint: disable=home-assistant-enforce-naive-now` suppression.

See the `homeassistant.util.dt.naive_now` docstring for details.

pr_title: Use SmartThings custom setpoint bounds for air conditioners
issue_title: SmartThings AC with null `coolingSetpointRange` ignores available custom setpoint bounds
issue_body:
## Description

The Home Assistant SmartThings climate integration can expose an incorrect temperature range for Samsung air conditioners when the standard SmartThings `thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpointRange` attribute is `null`.

The affected devices provide a complete, unit-bearing temperature range through the same component's `custom.thermostatSetpointControl` capability, but Home Assistant 2026.8.1 does not use those bounds. Instead, the climate entity falls back to generic `7–35` limits while retaining Fahrenheit temperature semantics.

This causes Home Assistant to reject valid Fahrenheit setpoints based on metadata that does not represent the device's supported range.

The behavior was independently observed on four physical Samsung air conditioners. All four devices use the same SmartThings profile family and expose the same capability pattern.

## Environment

- Home Assistant Core: `2026.8.1`
- Integration: SmartThings
- Device manufacturer: Samsung Electronics
- Device profile/presentation: `DA-AC-RAC-000003`
- Model family: `ARTIK051_PRAC_20K`
- `pysmartthings`: `4.0.1`

## Actual SmartThings representation

A sanitized representative device status contains the following values under the same `main` component:

```text
temperatureMeasurement.temperature
  value: 69
  unit: F

thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpoint
  value: 61
  unit: F

thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpointRange
  value: null

custom.thermostatSetpointControl.minimumSetpoint
  value: 61
  unit: F

custom.thermostatSetpointControl.maximumSetpoint
  value: 86
  unit: F
```

The same representation was independently confirmed on all four devices:

```text
thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpointRange: null
custom.thermostatSetpointControl: 61–86 F
```

The values were not necessarily sampled atomically at the same timestamp, but they are present in the same device/component status representation.

## Actual Home Assistant behavior

The Home Assistant climate entity exposes:

```text
temperature_unit: °F
min_temp: 7
max_temp: 35
```

A service call using a valid device-supported Fahrenheit target is rejected with:

```text
Provided temperature 61.0 is not valid.
Accepted range is 7 to 35
```

This is not specifically a `61°F` problem. Other ordinary Fahrenheit targets above `35` can also be rejected because Home Assistant is validating them against the incorrect generic range.

## Expected behavior

Home Assistant should expose a temperature range consistent with available device-specific SmartThings capability data.

When `thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpointRange` is unavailable or `null`, but `custom.thermostatSetpointControl.minimumSetpoint` and `maximumSetpoint` provide a complete coherent range, those device-specific bounds should be considered before generic climate defaults.

For the representative device status above, the expected climate metadata is:

```text
temperature_unit: °F
min_temp: 61
max_temp: 86
```

## Relationship to PR #178430

This appears to be a follow-up gap related to [Home Assistant Core PR #178430](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/178430), "Use SmartThings cooling setpoint range for air conditioners."

That PR added handling for `thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpointRange`. Its `da_ac_rac_000003` fixture has `coolingSetpointRange = null` and therefore remains on generic defaults.

Real `DA-AC-RAC-000003` devices additionally expose a complete unit-bearing range through `custom.thermostatSetpointControl`.

This is not intended as criticism of PR #178430. The standard-range handling is useful for devices that provide that capability. This issue identifies a likely additional representation case for devices whose standard range is null but whose custom setpoint-control capability is populated.

## Library evidence

The `pysmartthings==4.0.1` library already exposes:

```text
Capability.CUSTOM_THERMOSTAT_SETPOINT_CONTROL
Attribute.MINIMUM_SETPOINT
Attribute.MAXIMUM_SETPOINT
```

Its capability-to-attribute registry includes both custom range attributes. No raw JSON parser or Samsung-model hardcoding appears necessary.

## Reproduction steps

1. Add an affected Samsung SmartThings air conditioner using the `DA-AC-RAC-000003` profile family.
2. Inspect its SmartThings device status under the `main` component.
3. Confirm that `temperatureMeasurement.temperature` is reported in Fahrenheit, `thermostatCoolingSetpoint.coolingSetpointRange` is `null`, and `custom.thermostatSetpointControl.minimumSetpoint` and `maximumSetpoint` are populated in Fahrenheit.
4. Load the device through Home Assistant Core `2026.8.1`.
5. Inspect the climate entity attributes.
6. Observe:

   ```text
   min_temp: 7
   max_temp: 35
   temperature_unit: °F
   ```

7. Call `climate.set_temperature` with a valid device-supported Fahrenheit target such as `61°F`.
8. Observe validation failure:

   ```text
   Provided temperature 61.0 is not valid.
   Accepted range is 7 to 35
   ```

## Privacy review

The report intentionally excludes device IDs, owner IDs, location IDs, room IDs, timestamps, household automation details, credentials, and raw device JSON. It retains only manufacturer/profile/model metadata and the sanitized capability values needed to reproduce the integration behavior.

## Open questions

- Is `custom.thermostatSetpointControl` intended to provide the authoritative fallback range for SmartThings air conditioners when `coolingSetpointRange` is null?
- Should the custom capability be considered for all SmartThings climate entities that expose it, or only for specific device classes?
- Are the custom minimum and maximum values always reported in the same unit as `temperatureMeasurement.temperature`?
- Should an incomplete or unit-inconsistent custom pair be ignored and replaced by generic defaults?
- Should the existing `target_temperature_step` behavior also be considered when only the custom capability is populated?

pr_title: Send the transition with the WLED segment change
issue_title: WLED integration: light.turn_on transition not sent in JSON API request (tt field missing)
issue_body:
### The problem

When calling `light.turn_on` on a WLED RGBW light entity with a `transition` value specified, the integration does not include the `tt` field in the outgoing WLED JSON API request at all. As a result, WLED falls back to its own configured Default Transition Time (0.7s in this case) instead of the transition duration specified in the service call. This is not intermittent based on color values, brightness, white channel, or timing between calls — every on-to-on color/brightness change captured on the wire was missing `tt`, regardless of automation.

Steps to reproduce:
Create an automation with light.turn_on, targeting a WLED RGBW light, specifying rgbw_color, brightness_pct, and transition (e.g. transition: 126).
Trigger the automation while the light is already on (not from an off state — off→on uses WLED's separate power-on fade logic, which is a different code path).
Observe the light snaps to the new state almost instantly rather than fading over the specified duration.
Evidence (packet capture via port mirroring + Wireshark):
Automation action:
action: light.turn_on
target:
  device_id: <device_id>
data:
  rgbw_color: [235, 60, 10, 0]
  brightness_pct: 45
  transition: 126

Actual outgoing request body captured on the wire:
{"seg":[{"bri":255,"on":true,"col":[[210,190,10,0]],"id":0}],"v":true}

No tt field is present. WLED's response confirms it used its own default:
"transition":7

(7 = 0.7 seconds, WLED's own Default Transition Time — not the 126s specified in the automation)
A second automation (different action, different color target, same device) was also captured and shows the same pattern — tt absent from the request, WLED's response again showing its own default of 7:
{"seg":[{"bri":255,"on":true,"col":[[0,5,153,0]],"id":0}],"v":true}

Control test — confirming WLED itself honors tt correctly:
A manual API call sent directly to the device (bypassing HA) with tt explicitly included transitions correctly over the specified duration:
curl -X POST http://<device_ip>/json/state -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"on":true,"bri":115,"seg":[{"id":0,"col":[[235,60,10,0]]}],"tt":900}'

This confirms the bug is in how the HA WLED integration builds its outgoing request, not in WLED itself, the network, or the automation configuration.
Expected behavior:
The transition value from the light.turn_on service call should be translated into the tt field (in tenths of a second) in the outgoing WLED JSON API request.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.8.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

WLED

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

[config_entry-wled-01KXAQY0N2D4DKK218TNNVAX31.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30894397/config_entry-wled-01KXAQY0N2D4DKK218TNNVAX31.json)

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
action: light.turn_on
target:
  device_id: <device_id>
data:
  rgbw_color: [235, 60, 10, 0]
  brightness_pct: 45
  transition: 126
```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
No errors appear in the Home Assistant logs — the request completes with HTTP/1.1 200 OK and the integration reports success. The issue only surfaces at the packet level: the JSON body HA sends is missing the tt field entirely, which isn't something that produces a log error since the call itself succeeds.
```

### Additional information

Related issues:
[wled/WLED#2442 — Transition with Colour not working from Home Assistant](https://github.com/wled/WLED/issues/2442): reports a related but narrower symptom — the first light.turn_on call with a color change and a transition longer than WLED's default uses WLED's own default instead, but only on the first call after the color was last changed via the WLED GUI; subsequent calls transition correctly, and adding brightness to the same call transitions properly while color still snaps. This report's finding (complete, consistent absence of tt from every captured payload) is more severe and doesn't show that same first-call-only recovery pattern.
[home-assistant/frontend#22282 — Transition time not honored turning off WLED light](https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/issues/22282): reports light.turn_off with transition: 7200 (2 hours) causing lights to turn off within minutes rather than dimming gradually, on WLED firmware 14.3/14.4 — same underlying symptom (transition value effectively ignored) but on the turn_off action rather than turn_on.
[home-assistant/core#30488 — WLED light ignores transition time when on light.turn_on call](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/30488) (closed, fixed by [PR #30490](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/30490), Jan 2020): historical bug in this same integration where transition values were sent in the wrong unit (seconds vs. milliseconds), causing transitions to run 1000x faster than intended and appear broken. That fix also addressed transitions not being implemented at all on light-off. Included for context — this integration has had a units/transmission bug in this exact area before, so a possible regression is worth considering.
